MPTUNNEL.transport_selection: TCP uses three TCP carriers; QUIC uses one; TCP+QUIC uses both.

profiles.healthy: Shared 500 Mbps each direction; 70 ms DOWN / 30 ms UP; 25 s offered load; no injected loss, jitter or interruption.
profiles.independent: Three TCP carriers on one 200 Mbps link, one QUIC on another 200 Mbps link; 70 ms in the transfer direction / 30 ms return; 40 s load. QUIC transfer rate 10 Mbps nominally 15–25 s; UDP blackhole nominally 30–33 s. UP uses 70 ms upstream / 30 ms downstream.
profiles.loss-clear: QUIC 500 Mbps; 70 ms DOWN / 30 ms UP; 40 s load; 20% DOWN loss until planned profile epoch 20 s. Actual command brackets retained; no UP loss, jitter or interruption.
profiles.reordering: Routed shared 500 Mbps DOWN / 100 Mbps UP; 70/30 ms delay; 40 s load; initial normal jitter 20/5 ms clears at nominal profile 8 s. No injected random loss; queue drops and realized random sequences differ.

measurement_notes: Measured version labels identify builds, not a historical version comparison. One observation per configuration is not a confidence band or universal ranking.
All raw throughput bins are retained, including startup, zeros and UP settlement. Bin i spans [i*interval_seconds, (i+1)*interval_seconds); no trimming or smoothing.
DOWN is ordered HTTP body delivery during a time-limited partial-object transfer. First body includes application setup on running carriers.
Echo uses 64 bytes, a 500 ms requested sequential cadence and 3 s socket timeout. Points use actual request start; failures stay explicit outcomes rather than zero latency.

UP measures target-confirmation arrival, not API acceptance or instantaneous target write service. Exact natural FIN/ACK accounting and pre-teardown settlement are verified; no concurrent UP echo was measured.

Phase shading is nominal on the probe clock. Worker/collector and probe origins differ; applied_command_brackets are on the independent profile clock, not exact packet effects or exactly aligned probe times.

Egress counters include framing, acknowledgements, retransmission and copies across sampled windows; they are not exact payload-normalized overhead. Physical parent/child counters are not added together.

Matrix CPU is matched process interval utilization, as named. External-cohort CPU is final sampled process lifetime average. RSS is sampled residency, not proof of a leak or indefinite sustainability.
Loss/jitter clear is described by actual directional command brackets; first-observed state is separately named. No historical hardcoded clearance time is reused.
Browser smoke and platform tests are separate evidence; no browser throughput, UI value or cross-platform speed is claimed by these figures.
